messages:
ashley: Heads-up — after the INT8 rollout for rlx-13b yesterday we're seeing slow memory growth on long sessions and a subtle accuracy drift on a small prompt set. latency spikes correlate with KV eviction churn. Noticed more frequent 'page bounce' in the slab allocator traces. Anyone else?

perf-bot: [automated] KV slab usage rising: 87% -> 94% over 6h on node pool redwood-dedicated-3. Eviction events increased x4 since 06:00 UTC. Sample log: 
```
KV_EVICT: slot=13452 age=22s pages=3 precision=INT8 -> evicted
KV_PAGE_FAULT: hot_index=21 spilled_to_host=1
SLOT_COMPACT: skipped (low-free-frags=0.02)
```

sam: Repro steps? can we get a short repro session that reproduces within 10-20 queries? I can spin up an instrumented instance.

ashley: @sam yeah i have a session that reproduces reliably after ~1500 tokens of back-and-forth. I'll upload the prompt set to the perf bucket.

devon: Quick hypothesis: quantized INT8 reduces memory per KV page but increases slot fragmentation because encoded page sizes vary more, so allocator can't coalesce efficiently. That makes evictions more eager and causes reuse loss for long contexts. Also kernel selection is sometimes using the FP16 path for matmul while the KV is int8 -> extra decode/encode steps.

priya: Dug into profiler traces for a repro run. Top hotspots: memcpy (host<->device) during spill, quant-decode kernel (~12% CPU time), and 'compact_slab' runs that scan many slots. GPU kernel occupancy is good but overall throughput drops because of extra copies. Snippet: 
```
Profiler top:
  memcpy_h2d: 18.6%
  kernel_quant_decode: 12.1%
  kv_lookup: 9.4%
  slab_scan_compact: 7.9%
  batch_dispatch_wait: 6.8%
```

sam: So two axes: allocator fragmentation and extra decode/encode work in the hot path. Any telemetery on accuracy drop magnitude?

devon: We saw mean logprob per token drop ~0.9% on a narrow eval (dialog continuity set) when using the INT8 + current eviction thresholds vs BF16 baseline. Not huge but noticeable on regression alerts.

ashley: Important: we didn't change batching heuristics in this rollout but kernel selection fallback might pick a slower path when encountering mixed-precision KV pages. That could increase latency variance and trigger backlog-based evictions.

priya: Proposed quick experiments: 
- A: run INT8 but enable "precision-anneal": hot slots pinned as BF16 (keep cold slots INT8)
- B: keep INT8 but lower eviction aggressiveness (increase residency threshold) and run on same load
- C: enable on-demand compaction every N seconds (n=15) to reduce fragmentation

Config example for experiment A: 
```
kv_cache:
  precision_mode: mixed
  hot_slot_policy: pin_as_bf16
  residency_threshold_ms: 120000
  compaction_interval_s: 0
```

sam: I can run A/B/C in parallel on 3 nodes. Will include full traces and memory histograms.

devon: One more thought: kernel selection table needs an entry for INT8-KV + BF16-matmul to avoid encode/decode roundtrips. If we add a thin shim kernel that consumes INT8 cache directly we eliminate the decode cost. That needs ops change but could be fast.

priya: I ran a microbenchmark: INT8 decode cost ~0.6us per page; for hot repeated KV hits that adds up. The compaction scan is expensive because we scan 64k slots with a heavy cache miss penalty. If we also maintain a small LRU index for hot slots we can avoid full-scan compaction.

ashley: Risks: pinning hot slots to BF16 increases memory and undermines the INT8 savings; we need to measure unit economics. Also pinning must have an eviction fallback for long-term cold-down.

sam: Actionable plan: 
1) @sam run experiments A/B/C with same load and collect: eviction rate, page bounce count, mean logprob delta, p95 latency. (ETA 6h)
2) @devon prototype INT8-direct-kernel shim perf estimate + rough patch (ETA 2 days)
3) @priya add hot-slot LRU index and compaction watch (ETA 1 day for prototype)
4) @ashley evaluate results and decide rollback vs tweak.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: experiment-A -> redwood-dedicated-3a (image: canary-kv-int8-2026-03-18).

priya: Early result (A): eviction rate down 45%, p95 latency +6ms, mean logprob delta vs BF16 baseline: -0.3% (improved over full INT8 -0.9%). Memory increase: +9% on the node (hot-slot BF16 pin).

devon: That's promising — tradeoff seems acceptable if we can cap hot seats. Can we make pin threshold adaptive (pin top-k hot slots per session) instead of per-size?

sam: Experiment B (less aggressive eviction) reduced page bounce by 28% but mean logprob still -0.7%. Compaction off led to slightly higher fragmentation over 12h.

ashley: Conclusion so far: mixed precision annealing (pin hot slots as BF16) gives most wins for accuracy and eviction reduction at modest memory cost. Next step: make hot-pin adaptive and implement INT8-direct kernel to recover decode overhead.

priya: I'll open a PR with profiler hooks and the LRU index + metrics. Also adding a new telemetry counter: KV_HOT_PIN_COUNT and KV_PAGE_BOUNCE_COUNTER.

ashley: Thanks team. Let's reconvene after sam's full 24h runs. If the telemetry holds, we'll ship a controlled canary for the whole pool and update the rollout docs. :thumbsup:

sam: Uploaded experiment data to gs://redwood-perf/2629994321/ — will post summary once 24h completes.

devon: FYI I'm dropping a spike on the kernel shim into a sandbox branch so perf folks can review.

ashley: Solid. If anyone notices any regressions in prod in the meantime ping #incidents.

priya: noted. I'll add a regression alert for mean-logprob delta > 0.5% so we catch issues early.

ashley: end of thread — keeping this as the single source for the rollout/mitigation plan.
